title: Dimension at a point of a quotient of a polynomial ring over a field: n minus the difference of heights
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$ an integer, $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $I\subseteq P$ an ideal, $S=P/I$ with quotient map $\pi:P\to S$, $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q'=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, a prime ideal of $P$ containing $I$. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of a commutative ring $A$ let $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)\in\{0,1,2,\dots,\infty\}$ be the supremum of the integers $t\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_t$ of prime ideals of $A$ with $\mathfrak p_t\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Let $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ be the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Then $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$ (computed in $S$) and $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')$ (computed in $P$) are integers with $0\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')\le n$, and $$\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=n-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')+\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q).$$

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00P2 (label lemma-codimension, line 28270: for a surjection S' -> S of finite type k-algebras, dim_{x'} Spec S' - dim_x Spec S = height(p') - height(p)) applied to S' = P = k[x_1,...,x_n], with dim_{x'} Spec P = n (Lemma Tag 00P1, label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-field, line 28222, and Lemma Tag 00OP, label lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660); exactly the identity c = height(q') - height(q), 'in other words dim_q(S) = n - c (see Lemma 00P2)' in the statement of Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909)
